assertions.description: navigator.gpu is the entry point. Its presence says the browser ships WebGPU; it says nothing about whether a GPU is available here.
requestAdapter is the step that can legitimately resolve to null on a machine with no usable GPU, which is why it is asserted as callable rather than as succeeding.
getCompilationInfo is how a page reads the WGSL compiler's own diagnostics, which is the only authoritative answer about whether a modifier is accepted.

The feature: a fragment entry point returning @builtin(frag_depth) greater f32 must compile without errors. Skipped honestly when no adapter is available — the assertion reports false rather than pretending, because a machine with no GPU cannot answer this.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{if(!('gpu' in navigator))return false;const a=await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();if(!a)return false;const d=await a.requestDevice();d.pushErrorScope('validation');const m=d.createShaderModule({code:'@fragment\nfn main() -> @builtin(frag_depth) greater f32 { return 0.9; }'});const info=await m.getCompilationInfo();const scoped=await d.popErrorScope();return ![...info.messages].some((x)=>x.type==='error')&&!scoped;}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: The mirror modifier, for a reversed-Z depth buffer, must compile too.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{if(!('gpu' in navigator))return false;const a=await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();if(!a)return false;const d=await a.requestDevice();d.pushErrorScope('validation');const m=d.createShaderModule({code:'@fragment\nfn main() -> @builtin(frag_depth) less f32 { return 0.1; }'});const info=await m.getCompilationInfo();const scoped=await d.popErrorScope();return ![...info.messages].some((x)=>x.type==='error')&&!scoped;}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: The control: the pre-existing unmodified form must keep compiling. If this fails, the modifier assertions above cannot be interpreted.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{if(!('gpu' in navigator))return false;const a=await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();if(!a)return false;const d=await a.requestDevice();d.pushErrorScope('validation');const m=d.createShaderModule({code:'@fragment\nfn main() -> @builtin(frag_depth) f32 { return 0.5; }'});const info=await m.getCompilationInfo();const scoped=await d.popErrorScope();return ![...info.messages].some((x)=>x.type==='error')&&!scoped;}catch(e){return false;}})()

assertions.description: The modifier set is closed: a plausible-looking keyword outside it must be a compile error. Accepting it would mean the parser is ignoring the modifier rather than honouring it.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{if(!('gpu' in navigator))return false;const a=await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();if(!a)return false;const d=await a.requestDevice();d.pushErrorScope('validation');const m=d.createShaderModule({code:'@fragment\nfn main() -> @builtin(frag_depth) sideways f32 { return 0.5; }'});const info=await m.getCompilationInfo();const scoped=await d.popErrorScope();return [...info.messages].some((x)=>x.type==='error')||Boolean(scoped);}catch(e){return false;}})()
